result.detailed_feedback:
**Element Layout (13.5 points):**
The video uses a split-screen design with text on the left and animations on the right. While functional and clean, the layout is somewhat formulaic. Whitespace is managed well, ensuring the screen never feels cluttered, though the text-to-animation ratio remains static throughout.

**Attractiveness (12.2 points):**
The aesthetic follows a minimalist, dark-mode mathematical style. The color palette is professional but conservative. Animations are smooth and aid understanding, though the visual metaphors, like the squirrels, remain fairly basic in their execution.

**Logic Flow (14.5 points):**
The pedagogical progression is strong, moving from chaotic individual data to organized sampling distributions. It effectively scaffolds the concept by introducing the 'mean of means' before revealing the final bell curve, ensuring a logical build-up for the learner.

**Accuracy & Depth (14.2 points):**
Content is factually sound, correctly identifying the significance of sample size (n=30) and the emergence of normality. The depth is appropriate for an introductory level, though it glosses over some nuances of the underlying probability theory.

**Visual Consistency (14.4 points):**
Visual style is highly uniform, maintaining consistent fonts, line weights, and animation timings. The transition between static text and dynamic mathematical models is seamless, providing a coherent experience from the introduction to the conclusion.

**Overall Summary:**
This video provides a structurally sound and accurate introduction to the Central Limit Theorem. It balances technical information with accessible visualizations. While the presentation is highly professional and consistent, it lacks high-end visual flair, favoring a safe and clear instructional design.

**Key Strengths:**
• Clear pedagogical scaffolding from chaos to order
• Accurate representation of the 'magic number' in sampling
• High visual consistency and professional font usage

**Areas for Improvement:**
• Increase visual variety beyond the split-screen layout
• Incorporate more vibrant color accents to highlight key data points
• Briefly explain the variance reduction formula more explicitly

This phenomenon is described by the Central Limit Theorem, which states that as more samples are taken, the sampling distribution of the mean will increasingly resemble a normal, bell-shaped curve centered around the actual population mean.

C
The Central Limit Theorem states that as the sample size increases, the sampling distribution of the sample mean will approach a normal distribution, regardless of the shape of the original population's distribution.

C
The Central Limit Theorem requires the population to have a finite variance. A population with infinite variance would violate one of the key conditions of the theorem.

A
The chef is taking multiple samples (spoonfuls) to estimate the average characteristic (saltiness) of the entire population (the pot of soup). The Central Limit Theorem justifies using the average of a sample to make an inference about the average of the whole population.
